The Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection Screening Coverage Act (S.339) pours $2.8B into unproven blood tests while restricting coverage to those under 68. Early detection matters, but Section 2(b) ties payments to outdated stool DNA test rates, creating perverse incentives for labs to prioritize volume over accuracy.

The American Cancer Society notes these tests have 40% false-positive rates, meaning billions wasted chasing phantom cancers through unnecessary biopsies and scans.

Medicare should focus on improving existing screenings for breast, lung, and colon cancers where early intervention works—not fund speculative tech that enriches biotech firms while leaving seniors with higher Part B premiums.
